question: Should an independent OpenClaw owner accept LanceDB `existOk` plus the bounded three-attempt readiness retry as the memory-lancedb cross-process initialization boundary for the refreshed exact merge head?
rationale: The patch has direct local multi-process proof and no actionable correctness defect, but it changes persistent-store startup behavior and the protected label reserves final risk acceptance for a human owner.

options.title: Approve bounded dependency-native initialization
options.body: Accept the documented LanceDB create-if-absent contract and three-attempt readiness retry, then allow exact-merge gates to land the PR.

options.title: Require supported remote-store proof
options.body: Keep the PR paused until the same concurrent initialization scenario is demonstrated against a supported non-local LanceDB storage configuration.

options.title: Pause this implementation boundary
options.body: Leave the PR open while maintainers decide whether this plugin should use a different cross-process initialization contract.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded dependency-native initialization
recommendation.body: Accept the documented LanceDB create-if-absent contract and three-attempt readiness retry, then allow exact-merge gates to land the PR.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory-lancedb and release-history signals make this the strongest available owner-routing candidate for the persistent-store boundary decision.
